You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Are both giraffes rendered as chalk-drawn forms, including their contours, markings and body shading?
node.criteria: Pass if both giraffes' contours, spot patterns and substantial interior shading are visibly re-expressed as chalk drawing through broken or powdery marks, layered strokes, or form-describing rubbed shading. Inspect each giraffe separately. Outlines alone or a grain overlay on retained photographic interiors do not satisfy this condition. Fail if substantial portions of either giraffe still rely on photographic surface detail or modeling rather than chalk-drawn construction. Detailed spots, dark shading, accurate anatomy and smooth blending are permitted and are not by themselves evidence of retained photography. Return unknown only if the visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
node.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for the instruction 'Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk.' Inspect both giraffes' contours, necks, torsos, spots and legs, comparing interior rendering as well as edges. Assess the giraffes only; background treatment cannot substitute for their conversion.

node_traces.evidence: Both giraffes have altered, sketch-like outlines, but their spots and interior shading remain largely smooth and sharply defined, retaining photographic-style modeling rather than being substantially re-expressed with broken, powdery, or rubbed chalk marks. The background's chalky treatment does not establish conversion of the giraffes themselves.

d1_drawn_representation: The trace is valid visual evidence, not a transport or schema failure: it identifies broad smearing in the hills, sky, and ground and softened contours on the structure, while noting chalk-like texture and treatment on the giraffes. But its all-or-nothing fail does not explain the reference’s partial label: the edited image visibly makes some progress toward a chalk drawing, especially in the giraffes and vegetation, even if the environment is not fully reconstructed. Refine the binding to assess requested progress as well as completion, weighing distinct regions independently and distinguishing genuine chalk-like marks or shading from blur, streaking, and grain alone. Preserve the requirement that substantial environmental areas be drawn for a complete pass; do not treat incomplete coverage as no progress. Keep uncertainty for genuinely insufficient visual evidence, not merely because the edit is incomplete.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is too narrowly scoped to the giraffes to support the requested whole-image edit and the rubric’s partial-progress label. Keep the giraffe-specific check, but make its result distinguish visible progress from complete conversion: the edited giraffes have sketch-like contours and some chalk-like treatment, while their spots and interior modeling remain comparatively smooth and photographic. Do not collapse that mixed evidence into “no progress” merely because the strict completion criterion fails. Separately assess major environmental regions: the hills, sky, vegetation, and ground show broad smearing or streaking, which may indicate an attempted drawing treatment but should not automatically count as convincing chalk marks. Aggregate regional evidence so incomplete conversion can register as partial, while reserving a complete pass for substantial chalk-drawn treatment across the image. The trace is valid and visual; this is a criterion/binding and aggregation issue, not a transport or schema failure. Keep uncertainty only for genuinely unavailable or insufficient evidence."}
